content.text:
I need to build two new input grids matching that same pattern of scattered 3x3 shapes on black backgrounds—four corner triangles and four T-shapes, plus maybe some distractors—while varying the colors and positions. I'm analyzing the example's output grid to figure out how the corner and T-shape pieces are structured so I can replicate that layout.

Excluding colors 0 and 5 leaves just the colored shapes, and the background check confirms the cell diagonally inward from each triangle's corner must be 5, so I need to reconstruct each shape inside a 3x3 block filled with 5 except for the shape's color — covering the four corner triangle orientations plus the T-shapes.

Checking the top middle T-shape at rows0-1 cols3-5 matches a downward-pointing T from the input, confirming shapes occupy 2 rows within 3x3 blocks. Mapping out bottom, left, and right middle pieces similarly, then starting to check the heights of each triangle piece to verify consistent sizing.

Verifying the width calculation confirms the pieces fit together into a 9x9 output. Now I'm planning to construct new test inputs using the same piece set but with different colors and positions, designing a grid of 3x3 blocks separated by zero rows and columns.

Finishing the T-shapes: bottom T color 2, left T color 9 with full left column plus center, and right T color 1 with full right column plus center. I'm double-checking the left T against the connectivity condition, confirming the full left column satisfies the required adjacency between corners.

Now I'm laying out the full 11x15 grid, placing the top T, top-left shape, an empty block, and the right T across the first row block, then continuing with the bottom-right shape in the next row block.

Filling in the remaining row blocks the same way, then double-checking that zero is truly the dominant background color by tallying zero counts against the 5s and other values across all rows.

Finishing the row-by-row count of 5s and comparing totals: 5s add up to 44, while zeros and empty separator blocks add up to 96, confirming 0 is the dominant color. That means the argument color is most likely 5, since it's the next most frequent nonzero value.

Now checking the second input's structure: I'm identifying its corner and edge colors (8, 2, 1, 6, 4, 3, 7, 9) arranged in a 3x3 block grid with one empty block, and starting to map out the top row of shapes.

I'm filling in the remaining rows of grid values, then tallying up how many cells contain each digit—counting zeros in the separator rows and columns, then working through the 5s row by row.

The totals come out close (49 zeros vs 44 fives), so I'm considering padding the grid by adding extra empty rows to balance it out, expanding to a 13x11 grid before finalizing.
